title: Medical Entrance Examination
contentNote: A shortened demonstration using adapted NEET 2024 questions and SATHEE NEET/AIPMT question collections. This is not an official NEET paper. Collection year labels have not been independently authenticated.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: A 10 V cell has internal resistance 1 Ω and supplies a 4 Ω resistor. Find its terminal voltage.
questions.explanation: Current = 10/5 = 2 A; terminal voltage = 10 − 2 = 8 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: An ideal transformer has primary-to-secondary turns ratio 1:2. Find secondary-to-primary voltage ratio.
questions.explanation: Voltage is proportional to the number of turns.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: Which pair, like solid angle, is dimensionless?
questions.explanation: Strain and plane angle are ratios of lengths.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: In uniform circular motion, which describes velocity and acceleration?
questions.explanation: Both vectors continually change direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: For a telescope in normal adjustment, objective focal length is 140 cm and eyepiece focal length is 5 cm. Find magnification magnitude.
questions.explanation: Magnification magnitude = 140/5 = 28.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: A 10 kg object experiences a net force of 50 N. Calculate its acceleration.
questions.explanation: Newton’s second law gives a = F/m = 5 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: Masses 2 kg and 3 kg hang over a frictionless, massless pulley. With g = 9.8 m/s², find acceleration.
questions.explanation: Acceleration = (3 − 2)g/(3 + 2) = 1.96 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: A block rests on a 30° incline with static friction coefficient 0.4. What happens on release?
questions.explanation: tan 30° exceeds 0.4, so static friction cannot hold the block.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: A stone on a 1 m string just completes a vertical circle. With g = 9.8 m/s², find minimum speed at the top.
questions.explanation: At limiting speed, tension is zero and v = √(gr).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: Masses 5 kg and 2 kg are joined over an ideal pulley. Calculate acceleration using g = 9.8 m/s².
questions.explanation: Acceleration = (5 − 2)g/(5 + 2) = 4.2 m/s².

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: What mass contains 3.011 × 10²³ glucose molecules? Use molar mass 180 g/mol and Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³/mol.
questions.explanation: The sample contains half a mole, with mass 90 g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: Dissolve 5.85 g NaCl to make 500 mL solution. For molar mass 58.5 g/mol, determine molarity.
questions.explanation: There are 0.1 mol in 0.5 L, giving 0.2 M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.adaptation: Reworded for a concise demo; options may be reordered or supplied.
questions.text: A compound is 40% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O, with molar mass 180 g/mol. Choose its molecular formula.
questions.explanation: Empirical formula CH₂O has formula mass 30; multiply by six.

questions.text: For complete acid–base neutralisation, a 0.5 M H₂SO₄ solution has what normality?
questions.explanation: Each mole supplies two acid equivalents: N = 2M.

questions.text: Choose the forbidden (n, l, mₗ, mₛ) combination.

questions.text: Four bonds and one lone pair surround sulfur in SF₄. What is the molecular shape?

questions.text: Estimate pH for a 0.01 M weak monoprotic acid with Ka = 10⁻⁵.
questions.explanation: Using [H⁺] ≈ √(Ka C), pH ≈ 3.5.

questions.text: For exothermic 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), which change favours SO₃ at equilibrium?
questions.explanation: Cooling favours the heat-producing forward reaction.

questions.text: In Blackman’s principle, the rate of photosynthesis is controlled by which factor?
options: The factor in shortest effective supply
Every factor equally at every instant
questions.explanation: The limiting factor restricts the overall rate.

questions.text: After light saturation, adding light no longer increases photosynthesis. Which resource commonly becomes limiting?
